subject: Re: Aligning on pilot acceptance metrics and ops plan for Acero trial
messages:
From: Jeff Allen <jeff.allen@acerohealth.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot kickoff recap + sample payloads

Great meeting earlier — thanks for walking us through the platform, Connor. Quick recap and asks so we’re aligned before the pilot kickoff: 

Summary of Acero goals
- Reduce clinician query latency for chart summarization and coding suggestions.
- Improve retrieval relevance for our knowledge base (clinical guidelines).
- Keep unit inference cost within our pilot budget.

What we shared in the call
- 1k representative queries across three user types (triage nurse, clinician, coding analyst) — attached as acero_sample_payloads.json
- Baseline: current internal endpoint averages ~1.2s p50, ~2.8s p95 on 256-token requests.

Asks from Acero for POC acceptance criteria (we’d like Redwood to propose concrete gates):
- Target latency and throughput expectations for a production-like load (we plan ~30 concurrent clinicians at peak).
- Cost estimate per 1k tokens for the trial workload.
- Simple quality measurement rubric (clinical correctness / hallucination checks).

Timeline preference
- Start baseline test (Redwood runs) week of Aug 2.
- Joint evaluation & readout within 10 business days after baseline.

Attachments: acero_sample_payloads.json (application/json, 2.4KB)

Thanks — Jeff
Jeff Allen
Product Lead, Acero Health
jeff.allen@acerohealth.com
(415) 555-0283

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Jeff Allen <jeff.allen@acerohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff recap + sample payloads

Jeff — thanks for the clear recap and the sample payloads. Below is a concrete, measurable pilot acceptance plan we suggest; I focused gates on latency, throughput, cost, and quality so we can make a binary pass/fail call at readout. Happy to iterate.

High-level acceptance knots (proposal)
1) Latency (generation end-to-end)
   - Short queries (<128 tokens): 95th percentile latency < 350 ms.
   - Medium queries (128–512 tokens): 95th percentile latency < 650 ms.
   - Long queries (>512 tokens): 95th percentile latency < 1,200 ms.
   Notes: measurements are end-to-end (API request to final token). We’ll run steady-state and burst scenarios.

2) Throughput / concurrency
   - Sustained request rate: 20 req/s for the representative mix.
   - Concurrency: handle 40 concurrent sessions without degradation beyond +15% of baseline p95.

3) Cost targets
   - Target normalized cost: <= $0.0007 per token for inference during trial (based on mixed 50/50 short/medium workload).
   - Redwood will provide a cost projection table for 30/100/300 clinician-month scales during baseline run.

4) Quality (domain-specific)
   - Automated metric: top-1 answer agreement vs. golden set >= 88% (we’ll accept small variance by query type).
   - Human eval: sampled 200 responses across user types; clinical reviewer pass rate >= 90% (no critical hallucinations).
   - Retrieval/embedding relevance: MRR >= 0.78 on the provided queries for KB lookups.

5) Safety & compliance checks
   - No PHI exfiltration observed in red-team subset.
   - Audit logs enabled and accessible to Acero for the pilot window.

Gating logic for "pass"
- All latency and throughput gates met AND (quality automated metric met OR human eval pass rate >= 90%). If latency/throughput fail, we propose a remediation window of 5 business days to tune batching/quantization/routing and re-run.

Proposed evaluation plan & owners
- Aug 2–3: Redwood baseline runs against acero_sample_payloads.json and publishes latency/cost/throughput report (owner: Connor).
- Aug 4–6: Acero runs internal quality labeling on 200-sample human eval set (owner: Jeff / Dr. Sara Patel).
- Aug 7: Joint readout meeting (30–45m) to review metrics and decision (owner: Connor + Marissa).

Ops & artifacts we’ll deliver (attachments)
- redwood_poc_readme.md: instructions, test harness, and evaluation scripts (attached).
- baseline_metrics.csv: generated after Redwood run.

Next steps (short)
- Connor: kick off baseline run on Aug 2 and share initial metrics by EOD Aug 3.
- Jeff: confirm clinical reviewer for human eval (name + email) and confirm the 200-sample set by Aug 4.
- Marissa: we’ll loop in procurement for PO/SOW items if we proceed to reserved capacity.

Thanks — looking forward.

Connor O’Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai

---
Attachment: redwood_poc_readme.md (text/markdown, 1.1KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

- If the pilot shows promising economics we typically suggest a 3-month Dedicated burst window (reserve small pool) — we can price that once Connor shares the baseline.
- Procurement essentials we’ll need if you proceed: signed SOW, PO, and a short procurement contact for billing (email + billing address).
- I’ll open the HubSpot record and add the SOW template and procurement checklist: https://hubspot.example/ACERO-451

I’ll coordinate follow-up items once we have the readout.

—Marissa

Hi Jeff — Monica here from Customer Success. I’ll own onboarding and the evaluation template. A few requests to keep things smooth: 

- Can you confirm the named reviewers for human eval (we need contact + role): e.g., Dr. Sara Patel (clinical reviewer), and one operational user who will validate retrieval relevance.
- Please provide: expected peak concurrent users (you gave ~30; helpful if you can confirm 30 vs 50), and whether the dataset contains any structured PHI fields (we’ll treat accordingly).
- We’ll share a prompt-set template and the golden-label worksheet by EOD Aug 2 so your reviewers can start labeling immediately.

Operational owner matrix (draft)
- Redwood baseline run: Connor O’Brien (redwood).
- Quality labeling & clinical sign-off: Dr. Sara Patel / Jeff Allen (Acero).
- Contract & procurement: Marissa Cole (redwood) + Acero procurement contact.
- On-call during baseline: Monica Patel (redwood CS).

Thanks — I’ll drop the prompt template into the Drive folder referenced above.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

2) Any chance for a pilot discount or marketing credit (small) since we’re evaluating across multiple product teams?
